welcome_message: Create a Skyulf training project. First choose single_model for guided model setup or multi_target for independent targets configured in src/modeling/branches.py. Multi-target setup asks only for shared data and deployment settings; each branch owns its target, features, model, tuning and split. Multi-target scoring is not available. Column names can be comma-separated. Initialization creates local files only. Use --config-file for advanced settings; see skyulf-core/templates/databricks/examples/ in the Skyulf checkout.

training_layout.description: Training layout: single_model = guided model setup; multi_target = shared setup, then define each target/model recipe in src/modeling/branches.py (training only)

project_name.description: 1. Data | Project folder and Bundle name (letters, digits and underscores)

engine.description: 1. Data | Library used for training and prediction: pandas or Polars; both can run inside Databricks

task.description: 1. Data | What will the model predict? regression = a number; classification = a category

catalog.description: 1. Basics and data | Existing dev Unity Catalog catalog

schema.description: 1. Basics and data | Existing dev Unity Catalog schema

source_table_name.description: 1. Data | Training INPUT table: existing rows with features and known answers. Enter table name only; blank uses <project_name>_source

score_source_table_name.description: 1. Data | Prediction INPUT table: rows the model will read to make predictions. This is NOT the output table. Blank = same input as training

prediction_table_name.description: 1. Data | Prediction OUTPUT table name, e.g. customer_predictions. Results are written here; blank uses <project_name>_predictions

record_key_columns.description: 1. Data | Columns identifying one record, e.g. customer_id or customer_id, observation_id. Separate names with commas; no brackets or quotes

input_columns.description: 1. Data | Columns the model learns from, e.g. income, age, balance. Separate names with commas; exclude record keys and the answer column

target_column.description: 1. Data | Column containing the known answer during training, e.g. churn or claim_amount

training_version.description: 1. Data | Training table snapshot number from Databricks table History, e.g. 0 or 12 (not a model version). null = resolve latest once at run start; an explicit version pins that snapshot for manual and scheduled runs

split_strategy.description: 1. Data | How to reserve test rows? random = random rows; temporal = newer rows for testing and older rows for training. Default source: full snapshot for random, rolling calendar for temporal. Override training_window_mode in an init file.

test_size.description: 1. Data | Share of rows reserved for final testing: 0.2 means 20% test and 80% training

random_state.description: 1. Data | Seed for repeatable random splitting. Keep 42 unless you want a different split

stratify.description: 1. Data | Keep similar proportions of each target class in training and test rows?

training_window_mode.description: 1. Data | Which source rows to use? full_snapshot = all; fixed_window = dates you enter; rolling_calendar = recent complete months; auto = all for random, recent months for temporal

window_timezone.description: 1. Data | Timezone defining calendar month boundaries, e.g. Europe/Copenhagen. This controls selected data, not when the job runs

monthly_lookback_months.description: 1. Data | Total complete past months to read, including the final holdout. Example: 4 months with a 2-month holdout leaves 2 months for training

holdout_months.description: 1. Data | How many final complete months to hold out for testing? Enter 1 to total lookback minus 1; example: 2

event_column.description: 1. Data | Column containing when each record was observed, e.g. observation_date; used to select older/newer data

event_time_kind.description: 1. Data | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

event_text_kind.description: 1. Data | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

event_time_timezone.description: 1. Data | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

event_date_only.description: 1. Data | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

start.description: 1. Data | Earliest observation to include, e.g. 2026-06-01T00:00:00+02:00. Required for fixed_window; rolling_calendar calculates it for every run

holdout_start.description: 1. Data | Observations from this time onward are test rows, e.g. 2026-08-01T00:00:00+02:00. Older selected rows train the model; rolling runs calculate it

cutoff.description: 1. Data | Stop before this observation time, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00+02:00. This is a data boundary, not the job date; rolling runs calculate it

filter_unavailable_results.description: 1. Data | Do answers become known later? true = exclude rows whose answer was not yet available at the chosen time; false = use supplied answers

result_availability_lag_hours.description: 1. Data | When result_cutoff is blank, subtract this many hours from run start. Enter 0 to 87600; example: 48 excludes results available in the last two days. An explicit result_cutoff overrides this lag for every run

result_available_at_column.description: 1. Data | Column recording when each answer became known, e.g. claim_confirmed_at. This is a column name, not a date you enter

result_time_kind.description: 1. Data | How is this column stored? timestamp = database timestamp representing an instant; local_timestamp = database date/time without timezone; date = day only; text = a string. Choose yourself; setup does not inspect the table

result_text_kind.description: 1. Data | What does the date text contain? offset_datetime = date/time with Z or +02:00; local_datetime = date/time without an offset; date = only a day, e.g. 2026-08-10

result_time_timezone.description: 1. Data | Which location does this clock/date belong to? Enter e.g. Europe/Copenhagen or UTC

result_date_only.description: 1. Data | This column has a day but no time. May we treat it as the start of that day? midnight = yes, 00:00 in your chosen timezone; reject = stop if such a value is encountered

result_cutoff.description: 1. Data | Use answers known by this time, INCLUDING this instant, e.g. 2026-09-15T00:00:00+02:00. An explicit cutoff applies to every run; blank derives run start minus result_availability_lag_hours

max_rows.description: 1. Data | Maximum rows transferred into Python memory per read; exceeding this stops the run. This does not randomly sample rows

max_input_mb.description: 1. Data | Maximum input data size transferred into Python memory, in MiB (64 = 64 MiB). Model training can use more RAM

training_sample_rows.description: 1. Data | Optional sample: enter 10000 to select up to 10000 eligible rows BEFORE train/test splitting. null = no sampling. Prediction rows are never sampled

training_sample_seed.description: 1. Data | Seed for choosing the same sample from the same table snapshot. Keep 42 unless you want another sample

regression_model.description: 2. Model | Choose a regression model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

classification_model.description: 2. Model | Choose a classification model. It starts with its default settings; README explains how to change them

model_params.description: 2. Model | Optional JSON object of fixed model parameters. For voting/stacking, include base_estimators and any base_estimator_params or final_estimator to define the ensemble. Other models can set this in an init file or generated config

search_strategy.description: 3. Validation and search | Choose grid, random, halving_grid, halving_random, or optional Optuna. Core supplies a model-appropriate default search space; grid strategies evaluate its full Cartesian product

search_settings.description: 3. Validation and search | Use Core defaults for this strategy, or customize its controls below

search_max_candidates.description: 3. Validation and search | Maximum full-grid combinations to admit (1-10000). Grid and halving_grid run every combination, so preflight rejects a larger space

search_space.description: 3. Validation and search | Optional init-file override: JSON object mapping model parameters to finite candidate lists. {} uses the selected model's Core default search space

regression_search_metric.description: 3. Validation and search | Objective for choosing regression parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

classification_search_metric.description: 3. Validation and search | Objective for choosing classification parameters on training folds; separate from the heldout lifecycle metric

search_n_trials.description: 3. Validation and search | Trials or initial sampled candidates for random, halving_random and Optuna (1-1000)

search_timeout.description: 3. Validation and search | Optional Optuna soft stop in positive seconds; null disables it. A running estimator fit is not interrupted

search_random_state.description: 3. Validation and search | Seed for sampled parameter choices, separate from the heldout split seed and CV fold seed

search_factor.description: 3. Validation and search | Successive halving keeps roughly one in this many candidates per round (integer 2 or more)

search_resource.description: 3. Validation and search | Halving budget resource: training rows or estimator n_estimators. n_estimators requires explicit max_resources and a compatible model

search_min_resources.description: 3. Validation and search | Halving starting budget: exhaust, smallest, or a positive integer

search_estimator_min_resources.description: 3. Validation and search | Starting estimator budget for n_estimators halving (integer 2 or more; must not exceed max_resources)

search_max_resources.description: 3. Validation and search | Maximum estimator resource count for n_estimators halving; enter a positive integer compatible with the selected model

search_sampler.description: 3. Validation and search | Optuna sampler: TPE, random or CMA-ES; CMA-ES samples categorical axes randomly

search_pruner.description: 3. Validation and search | Optuna trial pruner; Core checks whether the selected model and validation method support early stopping. none disables pruning

search_pruning.description: 3. Validation and search | Allow Optuna pruning when model and validation settings support it

cv_enabled.description: 1. Cross-validation | Use several training-only folds to score search candidates? No duplicate post-search CV report. With CV off, search uses a training-only validation split. Final test rows stay separate. Defaults: 5-fold K-fold, shuffle enabled, seed 42; the following questions select the fold policy before the data window.

cv_folds.description: 1. Cross-validation | How many CV splits? 5 means five evaluations; more splits take longer (2-20)

cv_type.description: 1. Cross-validation | Fold method: k_fold, stratified_k_fold, time_series_split, shuffle_split, group_k_fold, stratified_group_k_fold, or nested_cv. Nested CV repeats an independent inner search in every outer training fold, then runs a separate final search Temporal CV automatically selects a chronological final holdout; its clock/window questions follow.

cv_inner_folds.description: 1. Cross-validation | Inner search folds for nested CV (2-20). Leave blank for the Core default. The strategy budget applies to every outer-fold search and the final search.

cv_nested_type.description: 1. Cross-validation | Policy at both nested levels; auto selects stratified classification or regression K-fold. Temporal requires a temporal final holdout and event_column.

cv_group_column.description: 1. Cross-validation | Group identity column, excluded from features. Final holdout isolates whole groups; disable holdout stratify.

cv_gap.description: 1. Cross-validation | Rows excluded before each temporal validation window at both nested levels.

cv_test_size.description: 1. Cross-validation | Temporal validation rows per fold; null uses the Core default.

cv_max_train_size.description: 1. Cross-validation | Temporal training rows; null expands, an integer creates a rolling window.

search_tune_threshold.description: 3. Cross-validation | Select a binary decision threshold from inner out-of-fold predictions. Requires probability output; final holdout stays untouched.

cv_shuffle.description: 1. Cross-validation | Shuffle rows for CV? Use false for time_series_split, true for shuffle_split

cv_random_state.description: 1. Cross-validation | Seed for repeatable CV splits. Keep 42 unless you want different splits

retraining_mode.description: 4. Lifecycle | Start training yourself, or enable automatic training on your cron schedule after deployment

retraining_cron_expression.description: 4. Lifecycle | When to train (Quartz cron)? 0 0 3 3 * ? = monthly on day 3 at 03:00; 0 0 3 1 1,7 ? = Jan 1 and Jul 1 at 03:00. Does not set the data window

retraining_timezone_id.description: 4. Lifecycle | Timezone for the job clock: Europe/Copenhagen means 03:00 Copenhagen time. UTC means 03:00 UTC. This does not change dates in your data

retraining_pause_status.description: 4. Lifecycle | Enable the training clock after deployment (UNPAUSED), or keep it paused (PAUSED)?

scoring_mode.description: 4. Lifecycle | Start scoring yourself, or schedule it independently of training?

scoring_cron_expression.description: 4. Lifecycle | When to score (Quartz cron)? 0 0 * * * ? runs hourly. This does not change the training window

scoring_timezone_id.description: 4. Lifecycle | Timezone for the scoring clock, e.g. UTC or Europe/Copenhagen. Independent of the training clock and source dates

scoring_pause_status.description: 4. Lifecycle | Enable the scoring clock after deployment (UNPAUSED), or keep it paused (PAUSED)?

model_change_mode.description: 4. Lifecycle | Keep old predictions and append new rows, or rebuild all rows into a new model-version generation

score_model_selection.description: 4. Lifecycle | Score with one pinned version or resolve the controlled champion on each run

promotion_policy.description: 4. Lifecycle | Require operator approval or promote automatically after quality gates pass

score_handoff.description: 4. Lifecycle | Optionally run the existing score job after champion initialization, promotion or rollback; score keeps its selected model policy

regression_metric.description: 4. Lifecycle | Metric for comparing regression models on separate test data (heldout). Lower error is better; higher R2 or explained variance is better

classification_metric.description: 4. Lifecycle | Metric for comparing classification models on separate test data (heldout). Some metrics need probabilities or specific class counts

min_improvement.description: 4. Lifecycle | Minimum metric improvement required for manual or automatic promotion; ties never pass

quality_threshold.description: 4. Lifecycle | Absolute quality gate; numeric required for automatic promotion or manual first-champion approval. Choose for your metric and task.

risk_category.description: 4. Lifecycle | Optional business risk label (e.g. Low, Medium, High); leave blank when unused. This label does not change promotion gates.

compute_mode.description: 5. Compute | Job compute mode for this project

spark_version.description: 5. Compute | Approved Databricks ML Runtime for the job cluster

cost_tag_key.description: 5. Compute | Approved cluster cost tag key, for example CostCenter or PayingRegNo

cost_tag_value.description: 5. Compute | Approved cluster cost tag value; for PayingRegNo, enter your paying registration number
